expectations.evidence: Summary table: Take (C1, C2, C3, C10), Decline (C4, C6, C8), 'Decline as written' (C5), 'Take in part' (C7, C9).

expectations.text: Accepts C1 (missing empty_table import), C2 (prose says 'both return 6' but the table has no 6), and C3 (with_serial alone is insufficient when several columns share state); the C3 fix points readers to barriers or the concept guide

expectations.text: Declines C8: does not propose enlarging the executed corrected example above the ~4.2M-row threshold (cites docs-build cost and/or that the page already explains the small size)
expectations.evidence: 'decline ... Cost. ... Four million-plus Python calls would slow the build and bloat the snapshot. The note at line 198 already tells readers ...'

expectations.text: For C9, proposes a corrected takeaway at tutorial resolution (e.g. 'treats formulas as safe to run in parallel') rather than enumerating the conditions or naming properties
expectations.evidence: '- Deephaven assumes formulas are stateless, so it can run them in parallel — this is fast but requires stateless code.'

expectations.text: For C10, verifies the claim against source (e.g. the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc: the engine may evaluate a non-parallelizable column out of order) and keeps the clause or asks, rather than deleting it or adding a hedge
expectations.evidence: Deletes the clause: 'C10 ... take. Nothing on the page supports this clause ... Remove both clauses'. The reply says 'I removed the clause'.
